about: Inspire Moore is a small family winery in Naples, at the southern end of Canandaigua Lake. Tim Moore fell for wine at twenty, worked harvests in Austria and earned an enology degree at UC Davis before he and his wife Diane opened the winery in 2007, in buildings that once served as a tavern, stagecoach stop and carriage house. Every wine is named for a virtue the Moores hoped to inspire more of, from Joy and Peace to Wisdom; this one is Rhythm.

Tim’s years in Austria shaped the cellar: alongside Riesling, the family works with Austrian grapes such as Grüner Veltliner, Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch and St. Laurent. The 2019 vintage carries a story of its own. Tim died that June, and his son Nathaniel, just graduated from the Finger Lakes Community College viticulture and enology program, became head winemaker at twenty-one. Nate favours native yeasts, a light hand in the cellar and wines that are not high in alcohol, and the winery still makes only about 1,800 cases a year.

Grüner Veltliner is Austria’s signature white grape, and in the cool Finger Lakes it keeps its brisk acidity and gently peppery side. Inspire Moore bottles Rhythm as a dry wine; recent vintages show lemon, green apple, white peach and a little white pepper, finishing crisp and clean. With a few years in bottle, as here, Grüner often softens and picks up rounder, honeyed notes alongside the citrus.
facts: Small lots, mostly native yeasts, minimal intervention
